searchText: cc <@498009160982724610> <@476250636548308992> Not yet sorry. It is in our to-do list however. I wonder if we want 5.1 for eth2 mainnet? I havent really looked into it yet on my end, is it incompatible with 5.0? no, the wire protocol changed, but the overal application logic stays largely the same. It's not a massive update and it isn't a small update. But the protocol is extensible which is really powerful and I think it would be worth it because it opens up options for all kinds of other utilities to be built on top of it. https://github.com/ethereum/devp2p/issues/152 has more information on details the spec in that document isn't 100% accurate, but the concept holds. And the wire protocol still has the same behavior as v5, just changes to the 3 different message formats. at this point, we'd need to consider an upgrade path (e.g. 5.1 falling back to 5.0 if the peer doesn't speak 5.1), right? at least if we rolled it out on, say, medalla one nice bonus in v5.1 is that it allows sharing the port with other protocols running on the same port (differentiation happening at the datagram level)
